# Rank-one normalizers generated by actual reflection representatives

For supplied `B : ValuationBuildingData G` over a nonarchimedean local field in
an arbitrary universe, this internal development proves that normalizer points
in the subgroup generated by two actual opposite root groups are products of
actual reflection representatives. The proof assumes
`RelativeRoot.HasOppositeFactorPairs B.i` explicitly. It does not supply that
premise or the structural centralizer-generation theorem needed for the
general simply connected translation-image equality.

The definitions and proof are derived from the published root-group
conjugation theorem, opposite-pair Weyl negation, and separation of normalizer
points from opposite root products. They are internal constructions, with no
additional source comparison claimed. Worker 1663 supplied the cell-stability
proof outline; Worker 1485 implemented it and the stronger normalizer
containment.

The subgroup `rootPairNormalizer a` consists of actual normalizer points whose
Weyl action sends `a` to `a` or `-a`. The subgroup
`rankOneReflectionNormalizer a` is its intersection with
`B.reflectionNormalizer`, the subgroup generated by all actual opposite-pair
representatives. It need not be generated just by representatives at `a` and
`-a`. Its associated set `rankOneReflectionCell a` has the form `U_a R_a U_a`.
Representatives at either root belong to the middle subgroup because their
Weyl actions negate that root. Opposite-pair existence and a nonidentity root
point supplied by the valuation also show that `-a` is an actual relative root.

Left multiplication by `U_a` preserves the cell by combining the first
factors. For `x ∈ U_{-a}`, the identity case is immediate. Otherwise a pair
gives `x = p₁⁻¹ m p₂⁻¹`, with `p₁,p₂ ∈ U_a` and `m ∈ R_a`. For a cell point
`u n v`, set `t = p₂⁻¹ u` and move `t` past `n`. If `n⁻¹` fixes `a`, its
conjugate lies in `U_a`, giving another cell expression. If `n⁻¹` negates `a`,
the conjugate lies in `U_{-a}`. Its identity case is immediate; otherwise a
second opposite pair gives a representative `m'`. Since `mn` fixes `a`, the
remaining conjugated positive factor stays in `U_a`, yielding a cell
expression with middle factor `mnm'`. Subgroup closure induction, including
inverse root points, now gives `rankOneClosure_subset_rankOneReflectionCell`.

If a normalizer point `n` has cell expression `u r v`, then
`r⁻¹ n = (r⁻¹ u r) v`. When `r⁻¹` fixes `a`, both factors lie in `U_a`;
their product is a normalizer root point and hence is the identity, using
`RelativeRoot.normalizer_eq_one_of_mul_opposite` with the opposite factor
equal to `1`. When `r⁻¹` negates `a`, the factors belong to `U_{-a}` and
`U_a`, so the same separation theorem at `-a` applies directly. Thus `n = r`
and `normalizer_mem_rankOneReflectionNormalizer_of_mem_cell` follows without
opposite-pair existence as an additional premise.

Combining these results,
`normalizer_mem_reflectionNormalizer_of_mem_rankOneClosure` proves the
pointwise containment. `rankOneNormalizer_le_reflectionNormalizer_map`
expresses it in the ambient rational-point group:

```text
N(F) ∩ ⟨U_a(F), U_{-a}(F)⟩ ≤ image(reflectionNormalizer → G(F)).
```

Here the brackets mean subgroup closure of the union, and `a` is an actual
relative root. `rankOneCentralizer_le_reflectionNormalizer_map` gives the
centralizer version by the published inclusion `Z(F) ≤ N(F)`. No simple
connectedness, Tits system, full apartment axioms, or integral-lattice
saturation assumption is used.
